rubric.why: Diffusion is the spreading and mixing of particles through a medium, from a region of higher concentration to lower concentration.
rubric.description: Defines diffusion as the spreading or mixing of particles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing particles spreading or mixing, or moving from higher to lower concentration; award 0 otherwise.

rubric.why: Effusion specifically describes gas particles escaping through a very small opening.
rubric.description: Defines effusion as gas escaping through a tiny hole.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that gas escapes through a tiny or small hole; award 0 otherwise.

modelAnswer: Diffusion is the spreading and mixing of particles from a region of higher concentration to lower concentration.
Effusion is the escape of gas particles through a tiny hole.

rubric.why: Oxidation can be described as the addition of oxygen or the removal of hydrogen.
rubric.description: Defines oxidation using oxygen or hydrogen transfer.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that oxidation involves addition of oxygen or removal of hydrogen; award 0 otherwise.

rubric.why: The example must show a substance being oxidised.
rubric.description: Gives a valid example of oxidation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid oxidation example, such as magnesium reacting with oxygen to form magnesium oxide; award 0 otherwise.

modelAnswer: Oxidation is a chemical reaction in which oxygen is added to a substance or hydrogen is removed from it.

items.followUp: Why does atomic radius generally decrease across a period from left to right?

rubric.why: Across a period, nuclear charge increases.
rubric.description: States that nuclear charge or proton number increases across the period.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that nuclear charge or proton number increases; award 0 otherwise.

rubric.why: The stronger attraction makes atoms less likely to lose electrons, reducing their electropositive character.
rubric.description: Links stronger attraction for valence electrons to reduced electron loss and electropositive character.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that electrons are attracted more strongly and are lost less readily; award 0 otherwise.

modelAnswer: Across a period from left to right, nuclear charge increases.
The valence electrons are attracted more strongly, so atoms lose electrons less readily and electropositive character decreases.
